title: U.S. Senate · North Carolina

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Thom Tillis (R) is not seeking re-election. Roy Cooper won the Democratic primary on March 3, 2026 with 92.0% of the vote. Michael Whatley won the Republican primary with 64.6% of the vote. Shannon Bray advanced from a canceled Libertarian primary; Michael Dublin is the Green Party nominee.

candidates.name: Roy Cooper
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 92.0% of the vote.

summary.text: Roy Cooper is the Democratic nominee for the open U.S. Senate seat. A Nash County attorney, he served in the North Carolina House and Senate, was state attorney general for 16 years (2001-2017) and was governor from 2017 to 2025. He won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 92.0% of the vote and is campaigning on affordability and his record as governor.

background.text: Born June 13, 1957, in Nashville, North Carolina, the son of a teacher and a lawyer; he attended public schools in Nash County, worked summers on the family tobacco farm, and graduated from Northern Nash High School in 1975.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 1979 (as a Morehead Scholar, according to Wikipedia) and a J.D. from the UNC School of Law in 1982.
Practiced law in Rocky Mount and Nashville, North Carolina, joining the firm Fields, Cooper & Henderson in 1982 and becoming a partner in 1985.

Elected to the North Carolina House of Representatives (District 72) in 1986 and served until 1991; appointed in 1991 to the State Senate (District 10), where he served until 2001, including as Senate Majority Leader from 1997.

Elected North Carolina Attorney General in 2000 and re-elected in 2004, 2008 and 2012, serving from January 2001 until 2017. In 2007 his office took over the Duke lacrosse case and dismissed the charges against the players.
Elected governor in 2016, defeating incumbent Pat McCrory, and re-elected in 2020. His administration negotiated the state's Medicaid expansion with the Republican-led legislature.
After leaving office in January 2025, accepted a teaching position at Harvard University, according to Wikipedia.

Announced his Senate candidacy on July 28, 2025, after Sen. Thom Tillis said he would not seek re-election. According to his campaign, he and his wife Kristin raised three daughters in Rocky Mount; he has taught Sunday school.

priorities.text: Repealing Donald Trump's tariffs, saying the constitutional authority over trade and tariffs rests with Congress.
Strengthening antitrust enforcement in grocery retail and food processing to block corporate mergers that reduce competition and raise prices.
Campaigning on his record as governor, including job creation and paid parental leave for state employees.

positions.summary: Says he will vote to roll back Trump's tariffs, arguing constitutional authority over trade rests with Congress.
positions.quote: The United States Supreme Court was clear that the constitutional authority on trade and tariffs rest[s] with Congress. I will vote to roll back the tariffs.

positions.summary: His campaign health care plan calls for reinstating the expired ACA tax credits and reversing Medicaid cuts.
positions.quote: Reinstate the ACA tax credits and reverse Medicaid cuts.

positions.summary: In a campaign statement on the Dobbs anniversary he said he vetoed an abortion ban as governor and, as a senator, would work to protect reproductive freedom.
positions.quote: fought to protect and expand reproductive rights of women in our state

candidates.researchNotes: Federal key votes and FEC totals are not applicable since Cooper does not currently hold federal office; his record above covers prior state offices only, drawn from Ballotpedia's summary rather than a full review of gubernatorial actions, which was out of scope at basic-tier depth.

candidates.name: Michael Whatley
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 64.6% of the vote.

summary.text: Michael Whatley is the Republican nominee for the open U.S. Senate seat. A lawyer and longtime Republican operative, he served as chief of staff to Sen. Elizabeth Dole, worked in the energy-industry advocacy sector, chaired the North Carolina Republican Party from 2019 and the Republican National Committee from 2024 to 2025. He won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 64.6% of the vote and is endorsed by President Trump.

background.text: Born October 1, 1968, in Michigan, and moved to Watauga County, North Carolina, during high school; his campaign says he was raised in Blowing Rock, the son of an accountant and a librarian. He graduated from Watauga High School in 1987.

Earned a bachelor's degree in history from UNC Charlotte (1991), a master's degree in religion from Wake Forest University (1993), a master's degree in theology from the University of Notre Dame (1994), and a law degree from Notre Dame (1997).

Began working in Republican politics as a high school student on Sen. Jesse Helms's 1984 campaign; worked as a federal law clerk in Charlotte and, per Ballotpedia, as a legal assistant for Sen. Paul Coverdell (R-Ga.).
Was a member of George W. Bush's 2000 Florida recount team and later a deputy assistant secretary at the U.S. Department of Energy; in 2004 became chief of staff to Sen. Elizabeth Dole.
Became a partner at the lobbying firm HBW Resources in 2007 and executive vice president of the Consumer Energy Alliance (2008-2019).
After President Trump's 2016 victory, led the Presidential Transition's energy, environment and agriculture teams, according to his campaign website.

Elected chair of the North Carolina Republican Party in June 2019, became general counsel of the Republican National Committee in February 2023, and was elected RNC chair in March 2024 and re-elected in January 2025.

Left the RNC chairmanship to run for Senate after press reports in July 2025 that he would run with Trump's support. According to his campaign, he lives in Gaston County with his wife Suzanne and has three children.

priorities.text: Public safety, including putting more police officers on the street and increasing their pay.
Supporting President Trump's agenda in the Senate.
Affordability, saying he wants North Carolina to be a place where people can buy a home and raise a family.

positions.summary: Says he wants policies that put more police officers on the street and pay them better, and that put dangerous criminals behind bars.
positions.quote: We need policies that are going to put more cops on the street, that are going to pay them better, and we need policies that are going to put dangerous criminals behind bars, not back on our streets.

positions.summary: His campaign issues page says he supports deporting people he describes as criminal illegal aliens and faults Cooper for vetoing a bill requiring sheriffs to cooperate with ICE.
positions.quote: I am 100% supportive of President Trump securing the border and deporting the millions of criminal illegal aliens

candidates.researchNotes: Whatley has not previously held elected office, so there is no voting or bill-sponsorship record; positions rely on campaign statements compiled by Ballotpedia.

candidates.name: Shannon Bray
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Libertarian Party primary.

summary.text: Shannon Bray is the Libertarian nominee for the open U.S. Senate seat. A U.S. Navy veteran who works in information technology and software development, he says he is known in the cryptography and blockchain fields. He has run statewide as a Libertarian before: for U.S. Senate in 2020 and 2022 and for lieutenant governor in 2024.

background.text: Born in Marrero, Louisiana; graduated from Thibodaux High School and served in the U.S. Navy from 1991 to 1997.
Earned an associate degree from Arapahoe Community College (2014), a bachelor's degree from Colorado State University (2016), and a graduate degree from the University of Delaware (2018).

Professional experience includes information technology, software development, information security, and management; he has been associated with the Coast Guard Auxiliary, the Naval Sea Cadet Corps and the Navy League.
Describes himself in a Ballotpedia survey as an author, speaker and professional coach living in Apex, North Carolina, with his wife and three children.

Was the Libertarian candidate for U.S. Senate in 2020 (3.1%) and 2022 (1.4%), and for lieutenant governor in 2024 (1.9%); he advanced to the 2026 general election without a Libertarian primary contest.

priorities.text: WFAE reports his campaign website lists digital privacy and civil liberties (including the right to use digital assets) as priorities.
WFAE reports his campaign website lists government accountability (including opposition to a government-controlled digital currency) as a priority.

positions.summary: In a 2024 campaign website statement (North Carolina governor race), proposed no restrictions on abortion through week 16, later limits that vary by circumstance, and prohibition of third-trimester abortions with listed exceptions.
positions.quote: Women have full rights to terminate a pregnancy up until the 16th week without restrictions.

candidates.researchNotes: Bray's campaign site (shannonbray.us) is behind a bot check and could not be loaded. The abortion position is from his 2024 North Carolina governor campaign site as quoted by Ballotpedia and may not reflect his 2026 Senate platform. He has not completed the 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. Priorities are WFAE's description of his website, not verbatim quotes. No other 2026 statements on the guide's issues were found.

candidates.name: Michael Dublin

summary.text: Michael Dublin is the Green Party nominee for the open U.S. Senate seat. A Raleigh native, Marine Corps veteran and retired public school teacher, he ran for U.S. House as a Green Party candidate in 2024.

background.text: Born and raised in Raleigh, North Carolina; graduated from Sanderson High School and served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1986 to 1988.
Earned an undergraduate degree from North Carolina State University in 1999.
According to his Ballotpedia survey, he taught public school for 25 years, including as language arts department chair at two middle schools, and recently retired.
Says he volunteered for 24 years in prison ministry at the Johnston County correctional facility, and co-chairs the Black Caucus of the North Carolina Green Party.
Was the Green Party candidate for North Carolina's 2nd Congressional District in 2024, receiving 2.1% of the vote.

priorities.text: A living wage of at least $25 an hour.
Cutting military spending and investing in healthcare, education and addressing climate change.

positions.summary: Supports a minimum/living wage of at least $25 an hour plus benefits, saying incremental increases amount to little real progress.
Supports single-payer healthcare, saying it is a human right that should not be conditioned on affordability arguments.
Lists addressing the climate crisis among his priorities and endorses the Green Party's environmental platform.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions are drawn from Dublin's 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, completed when he ran for U.S. House; no updated 2026 survey or campaign website statements were located.
